newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-SOME BIG NAMES FALTER IN FIRST ROUND OF OPEN.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-SOME BIG NAMES FALTER IN FIRST ROUND OF OPEN.

text.p: While Colin Montgomerie was shooting an impressive five-under-par 65 in the first round of the U.S. Open, many other top players struggled on Congressional Country Club's record-long golf course.
Seventy-five was a popular score for many of the big names as Congressional -- the longest course in U.S. Open history at 7,213 yards -- lived up to its advance billing as a treacherous track.

Two-time British Open champion Greg Norman, the top-ranked player in the world, Masters champion Fred Couples, PGA Championship winner Steve Elkington and American stars Davis Love and Phil Mickelson all posted 75s.
Briton Ian Woosnam, the 1991 Masters champion who had been playing well coming into this championship, carded 76 along with 1987 Open champion Scott Simpson.
Curtis Strange -- the last winner of back-to-back U.S. Opens in 1988-1989 -- staggered to a 79.
